chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr from Mihran bin Muhammad from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
I heard him (peace be upon him) saying: The singing is from what Allah said,
And from the people is one who buys amusing discourse to lead astray from Allah’s Way.

key_terms.الْغِنَاءُ: Singing or music, specifically melodic vocalization
key_terms.لَهْوَ الْحَدِيثِ: Amusing discourse or diverting talk, often referring to singing or poetry that distracts from truth

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on singing based on the Quranic verse in Surah Luqman?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies singing as a form of 'lahw al-hadith' (diverting discourse) that leads to spiritual misguidance, a ruling deeply rooted in the exegetical tradition where 'hadith' is understood broadly to include vocal music and melody. This narration from al-Kafi underscores the jurisprudential view that such art distracts the heart from divine remembrance, a concept further supported by the Quranic description of hypocrites who use it to divert others from God's path.

en.hubeali:
Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Mihran Bin Muhammad, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘
I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The singing (music) is from what Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Said
[31:6] And from the people is one who buys amusing discourse to lead astray from Allah’s Way’.
en.sarwar: Ibn abu ‘Umayr has narrated from Mehran ibn Muhammad who has said the following: “I once heard abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, saying, ‘music (and singing) are of the things about which Allah has said, ‘Among people there are those who buy useless things in the form of words to mislead people from the path of Allah.’”
